newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan fires ambassador to Peru over hostage affair.
newsitem.headline: Japan fires ambassador to Peru over hostage affair.

text.p: Japan fired its ambassador to Peru on Tuesday, forcing him to give up his post to take the blame for the lengthy hostage siege at his residence in Lima.

"We have heard yet again Ambassador Morihisa Aoki's desire to step down and after considering many things, we have decided to ask him to leave the post," Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda told a special parliamentary session on the hostage crisis, which questioned Aoki about his behaviour.

Aoki was sitting beside Ikeda when the foreign minister announced the decision to accept the ambassador's resignation, which had been regarded as only a symbolic offer that he did not think would be accepted.
On his return from Lima last month, Aoki told reporters he could not wait to get back to work and wanted to return to Lima as ambassador.

Aoki hosted an official reception at his residence last December 17 when it was stormed by Peruvian Marxist rebels, who took hundreds of hostages. Most of them, except for Aoki and 71 fellow hostages, were released in the weeks before the siege ended.
The crisis came to an end last month after a daring operation by Peruvian commandos who took the rebels by surprise during their daily game of indoor soccer.
Two commandos and one hostage, as well as all 14 rebels, were killed in the raid which freed Aoki and the remaining 71 hostages.
Aoki had become a centre of controversy in Japan for lax security measures regarding the reception and over his behaviour after the crisis.

He came under heavy criticism in Tokyo for chain-smoking during a news conference he held in Lima after he was freed and many Japanese lawmakers said his initial apology over security measures was insufficient.
In Tuesday's testimony in parliament, Aoki repeatedly apologised for his role in the affair and asked to be relieved of his post.

"I deeply apologise for the pain the hostages suffered during the crisis and especially for the deaths of the two military officers and the hostage," Aoki told the same session of parliament. "I am responsible and I have tendered my resignation."
"I especially feel responsible for the fact that we did not give enough concern to the possibility that the reception could become a terrorist target," Aoki said.
